message:
Amara, Baraka and Dalia, the proposal joins the box, frame, crates and agreed sizes into one buildable store.

The chamber is a hand-locked insulated box with room to move air around produce. Inner size 2.4 by 2.0 by 2.2 m gives 10.6 m3 inner volume at 27.1% produce fill in the chamber simulation (E44), small bedroom scale so air paths stay open, as drawn in the chamber sketch (E45) with fan flow in the cold room sketch (E32).

The box sits on a raised steel skid that also carries the solar rails and wind anchors. Spread floor load from one tonne is 2.04 kPa in the floor pressure calculation (E43), about one tenth of a person standing, so ordinary panels with plywood spreaders carry it, and the 800 mm door passes a person carrying a 600 mm crate.

Crates and power are matched by staging the hot harvest over three days. Fifty crates of 20 kg with 600 by 400 mm footprint ride on two side racks with a central aisle, airport luggage scale per lift, and staged load plus 315 W steady cooling in the steady load simulation (E31) gives about 8 kWh per day in the array sizing (E16), against 25 kWh one-off in the pull-down energy (E56). I am not ready, because door seal compression and rack guards with Dalia and the blocking energy mismatch with Amara and Baraka remain to fix.
